name: Line-retained toggling harpoon head
summary: A harpoon head that detaches on a line and turns sideways inside the animal, used independently by ancient peoples in Labrador, the Danube and Japan.
description: A penetrating point is mounted on a shaft so that it can separate while remaining attached to a line; tension can turn the head across a wound to resist withdrawal. This combination differs from a swallowed line-and-gorge device and from a point relying only on barbs. Bone, antler and other constructions vary; complete ancient rigging is rarely preserved.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: Made secure sea-mammal hunting possible for several coastal peoples, a small share of humanity, with later harpoon forms as successors; implies tier 2, below reviewed tier 1.

date.label: By approximately 7500 calibrated years before 1950
date.basis: Anderson describes the L’Anse Amour burial as approximately 7500 cal BP. A separate 2017 direct human-bone assay gives a marine-corrected median of 7714 cal BP, not a hard bound. The 1975 charcoal determination is uncalibrated. The archaeological head was not directly dated.

events.statement: A worked antler head identified as a toggling harpoon was included in the L’Anse Amour burial assemblage, supporting its availability within the represented local community.
events.scope: Worked antler head with a socket and lateral spur, identified in the excavation report as a toggling harpoon head; the line itself was not preserved.
events.population: Maritime Archaic people represented by the L’Anse Amour burial assemblage
events.caveats: The antler head and burial are archaeological evidence of access in this community; no preserved line, observed catch or individual use is established, and a ceremonial object is possible. The 1975 hearth measurement of 7530 ± 140 radiocarbon BP is uncalibrated; the separate 2017 marine-corrected human-bone median of 7714 cal BP is an estimate, not a hard endpoint. Anderson gives an approximate 7500 cal BP context. No world first, individual invention or cultural link to the European or Japanese witnesses is inferred.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 88 and 92: grave-goods context, artifact description and hearth charcoal
evidence.supports: Excavators describe an antler toggling head beneath the upper chest, a separate possible hand-toggle and a nearby hearth with an uncalibrated radiocarbon determination.

evidence.locator: Author proof printed pp. 913 and 927: calendar convention and L’Anse Amour
evidence.supports: Dates the burial approximately 7500 cal BP and identifies a toggling harpoon among the grave goods.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods, L’Anse Amour Burial Mound and supplementary figure S3
evidence.supports: Reports a direct human-bone determination with marine dietary correction and a 7714 cal BP median; the harpoon head was not directly dated.

date.label: By approximately 4000 BCE
date.basis: The 2022 synthesis assigns Pietrele toggle heads to the Gumelniţa occupation horizon circa 4500–4000 cal BCE. The artifacts were not individually dated in the inspected primary report; the bound is approximate.

events.statement: At Pietrele, worked antler heads identified as toggling harpoon heads were available in the local fishing and hunting assemblage during the site horizon.
events.scope: Antler heads identified by the excavation report as toggle harpoon heads within the Pietrele assemblage.
events.population: People represented by the Pietrele settlement assemblage
events.caveats: Archaeologists infer toggle function from artifact form and comparison with historically documented gear; no specific catch, preserved line or individual user is established for these specimens. Their horizon is contextual and approximate. A 2022 synthesis proposes earlier late Vinča examples, but individual identification, use and phase assignment require further examination; no world invention, independent origin or intersite transmission is asserted.

evidence.locator: Printed pp. 185–187 and figures 12–13; p. 181 settlement chronology
evidence.supports: Reports separate antler toggle heads and rod-shaped barbed harpoons at Pietrele; the settlement was occupied in the fifth millennium BCE.
Associates Pietrele toggle heads with an approximately 4500–4000 cal BCE occupation horizon; this is a contextual date, not a direct date for a particular head.

date.label: Approximately 5900–5650 calibrated years before 1950
date.basis: The dissertation assigns the relevant Lower Ento-a phase approximately 5900–5650 cal BP; these BCE coordinates are approximate conversions and are not direct dates of each artifact.

events.statement: At Sannai Maruyama, the Lower Ento-a assemblage includes heads classified as toggle harpoons, supporting their local availability.
events.scope: Bone or antler heads from Lower Ento-a layers, classified in the archaeological study as toggle harpoon heads.
events.population: People represented by the Lower Ento-a assemblage at Sannai Maruyama
events.caveats: The phase dates are contextual rather than measurements on each head. A specific target, complete rig and a connection to the Pietrele community are not established.

evidence.locator: Abstract, printed p. 1 table 1-1; pp. 36, 39–40 and figure 4-3
evidence.supports: Places the Lower Ento-a phase at approximately 5900–5650 cal BP and describes the phase-associated Sannai Maruyama harpoon heads as toggle type.
